newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes up as banks watch cent bank.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes up as banks watch cent bank.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed up against the dollar on Thursday, as banks stayed away from the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.45 after opening at 58.55 and falling to 58.63.

"The overseas weakness of the dollar, some big inward remittances and the Central Bank signalling that short-term depreciation targets have been met, have seen a lack of buyers," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
Some dealers, however, say signals from the Central Bank are the main reason for the dollar's slump in the local market.
So far this week the Central Bank has been lukewarm when the dollar gained overseas, while pushing it down aggressively whenever it lost ground, they said.
"If the Central Bank had stayed positive towards the dollar, banks would have bought the currency no matter what," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates, which were volatile due to a lack of sellers, closed around 12.5 percent after a big lender came on the market, dealers said.
